one_line: The Odia bhakti poet-saints who made Jagannath-centered scriptures and village recitation flourish in 15th–16th century Odisha.

appearance.age_look: early 30s, lean and agile but not muscular, with the calm bearing of a village scholar-devotee
appearance.face: Soft oval face with warm medium-brown Odia complexion, straight nose, gentle jawline, a slim black tilak on the forehead shaped like a vertical U with a central line, faint under-eye lines from long nights of reading, default expression serene and thoughtful with a small knowing smile.
appearance.hair: Dark black hair tied in a neat top-knot at the back of the crown (small rounded knot, not tall), sides and back short and tidy, with a thin cotton headband in muted marigold-yellow wrapping around the head and tied at the back, ends barely visible.
appearance.costume: A simple, fully draped Odia Vaishnava scholar’s attire: an unstitched off-white cotton dhoti wrapped ankle-length with a neat front pleat and a narrow marigold-yellow border, worn with a plain long-sleeved knee-length kurta-style angavastra tunic in soft light-cream, and a separate lightweight Odisha-style cotton uttariya (shawl) in pale saffron with a subtle red ikat edge, draped from the left shoulder across the torso and over the right forearm; feet in simple brown leather chappal-style sandals; minimal jewellery limited to a small tulasi-bead mala around the neck and a single thin copper bangle on the right wrist.
appearance.signature: A hand-copied palm-leaf manuscript bundle of the Odia Bhagabata, bound with a red cotton cord, held in the left hand, with a short wooden stylus tucked into the cord.

ref_desc: A lean early-30s Odia Vaishnava scholar with warm brown skin, neat black top-knot and marigold headband, wearing off-white dhoti, light-cream tunic, pale saffron shawl with red ikat edge, tulasi mala, copper bangle, and holding a red-cord-bound palm-leaf Bhagabata manuscript with stylus.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of a dignified early-30s Odia Vaishnava scholar-devotee: a lean figure with warm medium-brown complexion, soft oval face, straight nose and gentle jawline, bearing a vertical U-shaped black tilak with a central line on the forehead and a serene, thoughtful smile; hair is dark black, neatly tied in a small rounded top-knot at the back of the crown, with a thin marigold-yellow cotton headband circling the head and tied at the back. Dress them in fully modest, era-accurate 15th–16th century Odisha attire: an ankle-length off-white cotton dhoti with a narrow marigold-yellow border and neat front pleat; over this a plain long-sleeved knee-length light-cream kurta-style angavastra tunic; and over the upper body a lightweight pale saffron Odisha-style cotton uttariya (shawl) with a subtle red ikat edge, draped from the left shoulder diagonally across the torso and looping over the right forearm, covering the chest decently. Add simple brown leather chappal-style sandals, a small tulasi-bead mala around the neck, and a single thin copper bangle on the right wrist. In the left hand, have them hold a hand-copied palm-leaf Bhagabata manuscript bundle bound with a red cotton cord, with a short wooden stylus tucked into the cord, while the right hand rests lightly on the shawl or gestures gently as if teaching. Use a restrained palette of off-white, light cream, pale saffron, marigold yellow, and muted red-brown, and show front, side, and back views in consistent colours and details so this character can be redrawn identically.
